title: Veles native-bridge installer release descriptor
description: Schema 1 release identity and policy descriptor embedded in and authenticated with the signed maintenance carrier. Every field is required; unknown fields are rejected. Document limits: descriptor <= 256 KiB, inventory <= 4096 entries and <= 256 MiB, normalized relative paths <= 1024 UTF-8 bytes.

schema.description: Descriptor schema generation; only 1 is understood.

channel.description: Release channel. The channel selects host_name and bundle_id.

version.description: Three unsigned numeric components compared numerically, never lexicographically. The Rust validator (model.rs parse_version) is authoritative at runtime: it additionally requires every component to fit an unsigned 64-bit integer, which a regular expression cannot state.

source_commit.description: Full lowercase Git commit object ID (SHA-1 or SHA-256).

target.description: Release target; named as in config/tools.lock.json.

minimum_os.description: Lowest supported OS version. Production targets must be at least Windows 10 or macOS 26.0.

extension_id.description: Exactly one bare Chrome extension ID (32 characters a-p); the packaging allowlist in config/extension-ids.json decides which ids are accepted.

host_name.description: Native Messaging host name, selected by channel.

bundle_id.description: macOS bundle ID, selected by channel.

api_max.description: Highest supported host API generation; must be >= api_min.

payload_id.description: SHA-256 of the unsigned canonical payload inventory.

digest.description: A SHA-256 digest rendered as exactly 64 lowercase hex characters.

publisher.description: A trusted publisher/signer identity. The Rust validator (model.rs is_valid_publisher) is authoritative: 1 to 512 UTF-8 BYTES, no leading or trailing Unicode white space, and no control character (C0, DEL or C1). The schema deliberately states no pattern or character-length limit, because ECMA-262 \S and JSON Schema's character-counted maxLength disagree with those rules in both directions and a divergent second rule would become a second authority.

publishers.description: Trusted publisher identities; nonempty and unique.

denied_payloads.description: Payload digests that may never be activated again; denials accumulate.

rollback_payloads.description: Payload digests eligible for an explicit rollback; eligibility is the live/incoming intersection.

epoch.description: Monotonic policy generation. Relaxation requires a higher epoch and an authorized forward release.
